content: The baseline presence of drug resistance mutations has been linked to virologic failure, as demonstrated in a multicenter cohort study conducted in China. The prevalence and impact of pretreatment drug resistance were also evaluated in the 12249 Treatment as Prevention trial. Research has explored the cost-effectiveness of public health policy options in the context of pretreatment NNRTI drug resistance in sub-Saharan Africa. The WHO has issued consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, emphasizing a public health approach. Clinical trials have compared the safety and efficacy of raltegravir-based versus efavirenz-based combination therapies in treatment-naïve HIV-1 patients, with results published in The Lancet. Similarly, dolutegravir combined with abacavir-lamivudine has been studied for its effectiveness in treating HIV-1 infection, with findings reported in the New England Journal of Medicine. Long-term outcomes of dolutegravir in antiretroviral-naïve adults have been assessed, showing promising 96-week results in randomized studies. The pharmacokinetics and safety of dolutegravir have been evaluated in various populations, including pregnant women, neonates, and children, as part of studies like DolPHIN-1 and other clinical trials. Additionally, the in vitro activity of dolutegravir against wild-type and integrase inhibitor-resistant HIV-2 has been documented, highlighting its potential in managing resistant strains. Cost-effectiveness analyses have been conducted to assess the economic viability of resistance testing and universal antiretroviral regimens in resource-limited settings. Surveillance of transmitted HIV drug resistance has been emphasized as a critical component of public health strategies, particularly in regions scaling up antiretroviral therapy. The WHO has developed guidelines and tools to support the transition to new antiretroviral drugs, improve patient monitoring, and address suboptimal performance in quality-of-care indicators.
